anomalies.observed: On the FCC Peripherals sheet every PCA9685PW (U19) address strap pin (A0=1, A1=2, A2=3, A3=4, A4=5, A5=24) is tied to GND, which sets the 7-bit slave address to 0x40. U19 SCL=NET0053 and SDA=NET0165. On the Power sheet the INA219 (U4) is also on SCL=NET0053 / SDA=NET0165 with its own note 'I2C address: 0x40'. Thus two devices sit at address 0x40 on the same I2C bus, even though the schematic's own PWM-Driver note reads 'I2C address: 0x41'.
anomalies.expected: The PCA9685 should be strapped to 0x41 (at least A0 pulled high to +3.3V) as its printed note states, so that it does not collide with the INA219 current/voltage sensor, which the spec and schematic fix at 0x40 on the same FCC I2C bus (SCL=NET0053, SDA=NET0165).

evidence.quote: FCC Peripherals, U19 PCA9685PW: address pins A0-A5 tied to GND; note 'I2C address: 0x41'
Power, U4 INA219AIDCNR: SCL=NET0053, SDA=NET0165, note 'I2C address: 0x40'
Current/voltage sensor ... TI INA219AIDCNR, I2C addr 0x40 ... PWM/servo driver ... NXP PCA9685PW ... on the same FCC I2C bus

anomalies.impact: I2C address collision on the FCC bus: the STM32H753 cannot reliably talk to either the 16-channel PWM/servo driver or the INA219 power sensor, so servo output control and battery current/voltage telemetry both fail (the two devices acknowledge the same address and corrupt each other's transactions).
